correctness.rationale: A proper closed set leaves at least one vertex outside on each shore: a full shore would force all vertices of the other shore. With a,b selected on the two shores, each outside vertex on the second shore misses at least a-1 into the first selected shore, and the first selected shore has total missing-edge capacity da. This gives (n-b)(a-1)<=da and the symmetric inequality. The outside vertices also imply a,b<=d+1. If a>=2 and b<=1, then n<=1+2d. If 2<=a<=b<=d+1, then m<=a+db/(b-1)<=a+da/(a-1)<=2d+2, the last difference factoring as (a-2)(a-1-d)/(a-1). Neither case is possible. Choosing at most one vertex of each shore is sufficient, giving the polynomial and hull claims. At 2d+2 vertices per shore the given four-vertex construction respects the budget, and every outside vertex has exactly one neighbor in the set. The sharpness claim is for the common two-shore cutoff, not a separate optimal threshold for every unbalanced pair.
residual_risks: The supplied finite enumeration was not executed and does not establish the all-size theorem.

But that fact and its sharp witness are covered, and the remaining difference from the geodesic formulation consists only of counting all cross-shore pairs instead of the adjacent ones.
